correctness.rationale: The all-positive trace forces a linear forest. In the other direction, contracting the required positive components leaves a simple linear forest of forbidden block adjacencies. For four or more blocks an even-then-odd ordering along a spanning path completing the quotient avoids every forbidden pair, including the junction. For two or three blocks, any unavoidable forbidden pair can be made unique and incident to a nontrivial block; reversing that block permits the join. One block needs no join. The small orders, n!/2 maximum-support count, and marked component generating function check. Static shattering yields the adaptive lower bound, and predicting negative on unseen queries makes at most n−1 errors. The stored enumeration is corroborative only: the code checks all supports through n=6 and candidate forests through n=7; it was inspected, not executed.

originality.rationale: The distinct indexed Hamiltonian-cycle theorem already supplies the entire support classification by restriction. Add a new vertex x to K_n. Adding the two edges from x to the endpoints bijects spanning path edge sets of K_n with spanning cycle edge sets of K_{n+1}, and deleting x preserves every trace on E(K_n). For a forest with at most n−2 edges, the cycle theorem at N=n+1 applies in its |S|≤N−3 case. For n−1 edges the forest is a spanning path and, with x isolated in the support, is exactly the cycle theorem's (a,b)=(1,n) case. The converse follows from the same classification. This is statement-level coverage, not an inference about chronological priority from two same-day directory dates.
